newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natgas use to hit record 23.2 quads in 97 - AGA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natgas use to hit record 23.2 quads in 97 - AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas consumption should reach a record high 23.2 quadrillion BTUs in 1997, the American Gas Association said Tuesday.
The AGA said it based its year-ahead forecast on an estimate of 2.5 percent growth in the U.S. economy and crude oil prices averaging $20.50 per barrel.

In its base-case scenario, the AGA estimated 1.9 percent growth in natural gas use, off from 1996's estimated 2.1 percent growth rate. Estimated gas use for 1996 is 22.76 quads, the AGA said, up from 1995's actual 22.29 quads.

The AGA said its forecasts for record high natural gas use stemmed from advances in end-use technologies and market opportunities resulting from changes in regulations, including electric utilities restructuring.
Industrial natgas use should rise 3.5 percent to 9.25 quads in 1997 from 8.94 quds in 1996, it said.
"This increase is a result of continued growth in U.S. manufacturing, along with new gas-fired technologies that capture market share in this sector," AGA Chairman Tom Fisher said in a statement.
Industrial demand accounts for about 43 percent of all U.S. natural gas use.
Commercial demand should rise to 3.44 quads from this year's estimated 3.41 quads, partly on expectations for a return to more normal weather patterns after last year's unusually cold winter.
But the AGA said slightly lower demand for natgas in commercial space heating should be offset by increased penetration of natgas in markets such as food service and space cooling.
A return to more normal weather should produce a drop in residential customer gas use to 5.22 quads from 5.44 quads in 1996, the AGA said.

Electric utility demand should rise to 3.15 quads in 1997 from this year's 2.92 quads, the AGA said. But it said that demand could be as low as 3.0 quads if rain and snowfall persist in the Northwest, increasing availability of hydroelectric power.
